items.title: Solving equations using letter-numbers
items.explanation: To find an unknown weight in a weighing scale problem, frame an equation where the left-hand side (LHS) equals the right-hand side (RHS). For example, if one plate has 6 slices of bread and another has two unknown weights, the equation is 2x = 6. Solving this by dividing both sides by 2 gives x = 3.

items.title: Using trial and error to solve equations
items.explanation: When direct calculation is difficult, substitute values for the unknown into the equation to check if the LHS equals the RHS. For instance, in 2n + 1 = 99, testing n = 49 yields 2(49) + 1 = 99, confirming it as the solution.

items.title: Removing equal weights to simplify equations
items.explanation: If an equation has two identical unknowns on opposite sides of a balanced scale (e.g., 2x = 6), removing one instance of each unknown from both sides simplifies the equation to x = 3, making it easier to solve.

items.title: Solving arithmetic equations with letter-numbers
items.explanation: Arithmetic problems can also be solved by framing an equation. For example, if 14593 - 1459 + 145 - 14 = 13353, subtracting 88 from both sides gives 14593 - 1459 + 145 - 14 = 13353.
